Lutsk New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is Lutsk's New Jewish cemetery, established in the 1840s, serving a community first mentioned in 1388 and represented, alongside others, in the Council of Four Lands. Among its notable religious figures were Rabbi Shlomo of Lutsk, one of the first editors of Hasidic literature, and Yoel Halperin, known as Yoel Baal Shem; the Karaite scholar Avraham Samuel Firkovich is also counted among the community's distinguished figures. The Jewish population peaked at 24,398 in 1912; following the June 1941 Nazi occupation, 5,000 Jews were murdered immediately, and the ghetto's 1942 liquidation claimed 25,000 more. This cemetery was damaged during WWII and demolished by Soviet authorities afterward, its tombstones reportedly used, per local historian S. Shvardovsky, to build a stadium on Shopena Street; a memorial marking the former cemetery was more recently erected by Rabbi Israel Meir Gabbai.
